38.text: Jesus turned and saw them following. “What do you want?” He asked. They said to Him, “Rabbi” (which means Teacher), “where are You staying?”

39.text: “Come and see,” He replied. So they went and saw where He was staying, and spent that day with Him. It was about the tenth hour.

42.text: Andrew brought him to Jesus, who looked at him and said, “You are Simon son of John. You will be called Cephas” (which is translated as Peter). Jesus Calls Philip and Nathanael

43.text: The next day Jesus decided to set out for Galilee. Finding Philip, He told him, “Follow Me.”

47.text: When Jesus saw Nathanael approaching, He said of him, “Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit.”

48.text: “How do You know me?” Nathanael asked. Jesus replied, “Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.”

50.text: Jesus said to him, “Do you believe just because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.”

51.text: Then He declared, “Truly, truly, I tell you, you will all see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”

4.text: “Woman, what is that to you and to Me?” Jesus replied. “My hour has not yet come.”

7.text: Jesus told the servants, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them to the brim.

8.text: “Now draw some out,” He said, “and take it to the master of the banquet.” They did so,

16.text: To those selling doves He said, “Get these out of here! How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!”

19.text: Jesus answered, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again.”

3.text: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again. ”

5.text: Jesus answered, “Truly, truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless he is born of water and the Spirit.

6.text: Flesh is born of flesh, but spirit is born of the Spirit.

7.text: Do not be amazed that I said, ‘You must be born again.’

8.text: The wind blows where it wishes. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.”

10.text: “You are Israel’s teacher,” said Jesus, “and you do not understand these things?

11.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, we speak of what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, and yet you people do not accept our testimony.

12.text: If I have told you about earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things?

13.text: No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven— the Son of Man.

14.text: Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,

15.text: that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life.

16.text: For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that everyone who believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life.

17.text: For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through Him.

18.text: Whoever believes in Him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe has already been condemned, because he has not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son.

19.text: And this is the verdict: The Light has come into the world, but men loved the darkness rather than the Light because their deeds were evil.

20.text: Everyone who does evil hates the Light, and does not come into the Light for fear that his deeds will be exposed.

21.text: But whoever practices the truth comes into the Light, so that it may be seen clearly that what he has done has been accomplished in God.” John’s Testimony about Jesus

7.text: When a Samaritan woman came to draw water, Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink.”

10.text: Jesus answered, “If you knew the gift of God and who is asking you for a drink, you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”

13.text: Jesus said to her, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.

14.text: But whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life.”

16.text: Jesus told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.”

17.text: “I have no husband,” the woman replied. Jesus said to her, “You are correct to say that you have no husband.

18.text: In fact, you have had five husbands, and the man you now have is not your husband. You have spoken truthfully.”

21.text: “Believe Me, woman,” Jesus replied, “a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.

22.text: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we do know, for salvation is from the Jews.

23.text: But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.

24.text: God is Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”

26.text: Jesus answered, “I who speak to you am He.” The Disciples Return and Marvel

32.text: But He told them, “I have food to eat that you know nothing about.”

34.text: Jesus explained, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me and to finish His work.

35.text: Do you not say, ‘There are still four months until the harvest’? I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are ripe for harvest.

36.text: Already the reaper draws his wages and gathers a crop for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.

37.text: For in this case the saying ‘One sows and another reaps’ is true.

38.text: I sent you to reap what you have not worked for; others have done the hard work, and now you have taken up their labor.” Many Samaritans Believe

48.text: Jesus said to him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe.”

50.text: “Go,” said Jesus. “Your son will live.” The man took Jesus at His word and departed.

53.text: Then the father realized that this was the very hour in which Jesus had told him, “Your son will live.” And he and all his household believed.

6.text: When Jesus saw him lying there and realized that he had spent a long time in this condition, He asked him, “Do you want to get well?”

8.text: Then Jesus told him, “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.”

14.text: Afterward, Jesus found the man at the temple and said to him, “See, you have been made well. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you.”

17.text: But Jesus answered them, “To this very day My Father is at His work, and I too am working.”

19.text: So Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing by Himself, unless He sees the Father doing it. For whatever the Father does, the Son also does.

20.text: The Father loves the Son and shows Him all He does. And to your amazement, He will show Him even greater works than these.

21.text: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wishes.

22.text: Furthermore, the Father judges no one, but has assigned all judgment to the Son,

23.text: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.

24.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life and will not come under judgment. Indeed, he has crossed over from death to life.

25.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, the hour is coming and has now come when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.

26.text: For as the Father has life in Himself, so also He has granted the Son to have life in Himself.

27.text: And He has given Him authority to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man.

28.text: Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming when all who are in their graves will hear His voice

29.text: and come out — those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.

30.text: I can do nothing by Myself; I judge only as I hear. And My judgment is just, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me. Testimonies about Jesus

31.text: If I testify about Myself, My testimony is not valid.

32.text: There is another who testifies about Me, and I know that His testimony about Me is valid.

33.text: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.

34.text: Even though I do not accept human testimony, I say these things so that you may be saved.

35.text: John was a lamp that burned and gave light, and you were willing for a season to bask in his light.

36.text: But I have testimony more substantial than that of John. For the works that the Father has given Me to accomplish — the very works I am doing — testify about Me that the Father has sent Me.

37.text: And the Father who sent Me has Himself testified about Me. You have never heard His voice nor seen His form,

38.text: nor does His word abide in you, because you do not believe the One He sent. The Witness of Scripture ( Luke 16:19–31|LUK 16:19-31 )

39.text: You pore over the Scriptures because you presume that by them you possess eternal life. These are the very words that testify about Me,

40.text: yet you refuse to come to Me to have life.

41.text: I do not accept glory from men,

42.text: but I know you, that you do not have the love of God within you.

43.text: I have come in My Father’s name, and you have not received Me; but if someone else comes in his own name, you will receive him.

44.text: How can you believe if you accept glory from one another, yet do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?

45.text: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. Your accuser is Moses, in whom you have put your hope.

46.text: If you had believed Moses, you would believe Me, because he wrote about Me.

47.text: But since you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?”

5.text: When Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming toward Him, He said to Philip, “Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?”

10.text: “Have the people sit down,” Jesus said. Now there was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down, about five thousand of them.

12.text: And when everyone was full, He said to His disciples, “Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted.”

20.text: But Jesus spoke up: “It is I; do not be afraid.”

26.text: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it is not because you saw these signs that you are looking for Me, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.

27.text: Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has placed His seal of approval.”

29.text: Jesus replied, “The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent.”

32.text: Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but it is My Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.

33.text: For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”

35.text: Jesus answered, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me will never hunger, and whoever believes in Me will never thirst.

36.text: But as I stated, you have seen Me and still you do not believe.

37.text: Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will never drive away.

38.text: For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but to do the will of Him who sent Me.

39.text: And this is the will of Him who sent Me, that I shall lose none of those He has given Me, but raise them up at the last day.

40.text: For it is My Father’s will that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in Him shall have eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.”

44.text: “No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him, and I will raise him up at the last day.

45.text: It is written in the Prophets: ‘And they will all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard the Father and learned from Him comes to Me —

46.text: not that anyone has seen the Father except the One who is from God; only He has seen the Father.

47.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, he who believes has eternal life.

48.text: I am the bread of life.

49.text: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, yet they died.

50.text: This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.

51.text: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh.”

53.text: So Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you.

54.text: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.

55.text: For My flesh is real food, and My blood is real drink.

56.text: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him.

57.text: Just as the living Father sent Me and I live because of the Father, so also the one who feeds on Me will live because of Me.

58.text: This is the bread that came down from heaven. Unlike your fathers, who ate the manna and died, the one who eats this bread will live forever.” Many Disciples Turn Back ( Matthew 8:18–22|MAT 8:18-22; Luke 9:57–62|LUK 9:57-62; Luke 14:25–33|LUK 14:25-33 )

61.text: Aware that His disciples were grumbling about this teaching, Jesus asked them, “ Does this offend you?

62.text: Then what will happen if you see the Son of Man ascend to where He was before?

63.text: The Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life.

64.text: However, there are some of you who do not believe.” (For Jesus had known from the beginning which of them did not believe and who would betray Him.)

65.text: Then Jesus said, “This is why I told you that no one can come to Me unless the Father has granted it to him.”

67.text: So Jesus asked the Twelve, “Do you want to leave too?”

70.text: Jesus answered them, “ Have I not chosen you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil!”

6.text: Therefore Jesus told them, “Although your time is always at hand, My time has not yet come.

7.text: The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify that its works are evil.

8.text: Go up to the feast on your own. I am not going up to this feast, because My time has not yet come.”

16.text: “My teaching is not My own,” Jesus replied. “ It comes from Him who sent Me.

17.text: If anyone desires to do His will, he will know whether My teaching is from God or whether I speak on My own.

18.text: He who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory, but He who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him is a man of truth; in Him there is no falsehood.

19.text: Has not Moses given you the law? Yet not one of you keeps it. Why are you trying to kill Me?”

21.text: Jesus answered them, “I did one miracle, and you are all amazed.

22.text: But because Moses gave you circumcision, you circumcise a boy on the Sabbath (not that it is from Moses, but from the patriarchs.)

23.text: If a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses will not be broken, why are you angry with Me for making the whole man well on the Sabbath?

24.text: Stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly.” Is Jesus the Christ?

28.text: Then Jesus, still teaching in the temple courts, cried out, “You know Me, and you know where I am from. I have not come of My own accord, but He who sent Me is true. You do not know Him,

29.text: but I know Him, because I am from Him and He sent Me.”

33.text: So Jesus said, “I am with you only a little while longer, and then I am going to the One who sent Me.

34.text: You will look for Me, but you will not find Me; and where I am, you cannot come.”

37.text: On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood up and called out in a loud voice, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.

38.text: Whoever believes in Me, as the Scripture has said: ‘Streams of living water will flow from within him.’”

12.text: Once again, Jesus spoke to the people and said, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”

21.text: Again He said to them, “I am going away, and you will look for Me, but you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”

23.text: Then He told them, “You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world.

24.text: That is why I told you that you would die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins.”

28.text: So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He, and that I do nothing on My own, but speak exactly what the Father has taught Me.

31.text: So He said to the Jews who had believed Him, “If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples.

32.text: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”

34.text: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who sins is a slave to sin.

36.text: So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.

51.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps My word, he will never see death.”

56.text: Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad.”

58.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you,” Jesus declared, “before Abraham was born, I am! ”

3.text: Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him.

4.text: While it is daytime, we must do the works of Him who sent Me. Night is coming, when no one can work.

5.text: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”

7.text: Then He told him, “Go, wash in the Pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So the man went and washed, and came back seeing.

35.text: When Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, He found the man and said, “ Do you believe in the Son of Man?”

37.text: “You have already seen Him,” Jesus answered. “He is the One speaking with you.”

39.text: Then Jesus declared, “For judgment I have come into this world, so that the blind may see and those who see may become blind.”

41.text: “If you were blind,” Jesus replied, “you would not be guilty of sin. But since you claim you can see, your guilt remains.”

1.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the gate, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber.

2.text: But the one who enters by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.

3.text: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen for his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.

4.text: When he has brought out all his own, he goes on ahead of them, and his sheep follow him because they know his voice.

5.text: But they will never follow a stranger; in fact, they will flee from him because they do not recognize his voice.”

7.text: So He said to them again, “Truly, truly, I tell you, I am the gate for the sheep.

8.text: All who came before Me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.

9.text: I am the gate. If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved. He will come in and go out and find pasture.

10.text: The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I have come that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness.

11.text: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.

12.text: The hired hand is not the shepherd, and the sheep are not his own. When he sees the wolf coming, he abandons the sheep and runs away. Then the wolf pounces on them and scatters the flock.

13.text: The man runs away because he is a hired servant and is unconcerned for the sheep.

14.text: I am the good shepherd. I know My sheep and My sheep know Me,

15.text: just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father. And I lay down My life for the sheep.

16.text: I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.

17.text: The reason the Father loves Me is that I lay down My life in order to take it up again.

18.text: No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of My own accord. I have authority to lay it down and authority to take it up again. This charge I have received from My Father.”

25.text: “I already told you,” Jesus replied, “but you did not believe. The works I do in My Father’s name testify on My behalf.

26.text: But because you are not My sheep, you refuse to believe.

27.text: My sheep listen to My voice; I know them, and they follow Me.

28.text: I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one can snatch them out of My hand.

29.text: My Father who has given them to Me is greater than all. No one can snatch them out of My Father’s hand.

30.text: I and the Father are one.”

32.text: But Jesus responded, “I have shown you many good works from the Father. For which of these do you stone Me?”

34.text: Jesus replied, “Is it not written in your Law: ‘I have said you are gods’?

35.text: If he called them gods to whom the word of God came — and the Scripture cannot be broken —

36.text: then what about the One whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world? How then can you accuse Me of blasphemy for stating that I am the Son of God?

37.text: If I am not doing the works of My Father, then do not believe Me.

38.text: But if I am doing them, even though you do not believe Me, believe the works themselves, so that you may know and understand that the Father is in Me, and I am in the Father.”

4.text: When Jesus heard this, He said, “This sickness will not end in death. No, it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”

7.text: and then He said to the disciples, “Let us go back to Judea.”

9.text: Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours of daylight? If anyone walks in the daytime, he will not stumble, because he sees by the light of this world.

10.text: But if anyone walks at night, he will stumble, because he has no light.”

11.text: After He had said this, He told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.”

14.text: So Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus is dead,

15.text: and for your sake I am glad I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him.”

23.text: “Your brother will rise again,” Jesus told her.

25.text: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies.

26.text: And everyone who lives and believes in Me will never die. Do you believe this?”

34.text: “Where have you put him?” He asked. “Come and see, Lord,” they answered.

39.text: “Take away the stone,” Jesus said. “Lord, by now he stinks,” said Martha, the sister of the dead man. “It has already been four days.”

40.text: Jesus replied, “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?”

41.text: So they took away the stone. Then Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said, “Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.

42.text: I knew that You always hear Me, but I say this for the benefit of the people standing here, so they may believe that You sent Me.”

43.text: After Jesus had said this, He called out in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”

44.text: The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen, and his face wrapped in a cloth. “Unwrap him and let him go,” Jesus told them. The Plot to Kill Jesus ( Matthew 26:1–5|MAT 26:1-5; Mark 14:1–2|MRK 14:1-2; Luke 22:1–2|LUK 22:1-2 )
